subject: Nested enclave provisioning & contract prioritization for renewal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Gina Torres <gina@cedarline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Nested enclave provisioning & contract prioritization for renewal

Hi Gina —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, Cedarline's renewal (current term ends 2028-07-31) is a good opportunity to: add two isolated on‑prem enclaves in the EMEA lab cluster, increase standby capacity for your analytics workloads by ~60% (burst+standby), and align term and billing to a 24‑month committed cadence.

Attached are the initial artifacts: proposed-sow.pdf (high-level scope & delivery milestones) and capacity-matrix.xlsx (requested nodes / expected QPS / estimated token volumes). Key asks from our side so we can prioritize your provisioning in June: 
- Confirmation that the two EMEA lab sites will be treated as isolated enclaves (no cross‑tenant KV cache).
- Confirmation of preferred contract term (12 v 24 months) and whether Cedarline wants the standby nodes billed as reserved or metered burst.
- Any procurement deadlines for July cutover.

If you can confirm those three items, we’ll elevate the order to our Private rollout queue and issue a prioritized SOW+pricing packet by Monday. If procurement needs the DocuSign link earlier, say the word and we’ll provision a draft for signature.

Thanks — looking forward to locking timelines.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com]

---
Attachment stubs: proposed-sow.pdf (PDF), capacity-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Gina Torres <gina@cedarline.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@cedarline.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nested enclave provisioning & contract prioritization for renewal

Jordan —

Appreciate the recap and the docs. Quick clarifications from our side:
1) Yes, both lab sites must be fully isolated (PHI processing in one, de‑identified analytics in the other) — isolation is non‑negotiable.
2) Procurement prefers a 24‑month committed term but we need an option that amortizes standby capacity across the term (we'd like to see reserved pricing with a seasonal burst buffer).
3) Procurement deadline: leadership wants a signed agreement by 2028‑06‑28 to align with our fiscal planning.

Two questions before you escalate: what is the expected lead time for hardware/network changes on our side (we own rack/power/cabling) and are there any maintenance blackout windows we should know about for the proposed on‑prem agents?

Cc'd procurement to weigh in on PO process.

Thanks —
Gina
Head of Platform Ops, Cedarline Analytics
gina@cedarline.com

---
Note: Procurecc will respond separately about PO timelines.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Gina Torres <gina@cedarline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procure@cedarline.com>
Date: 2028-05-24T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nested enclave provisioning & contract prioritization for renewal

Gina — great, thanks for the clear direction. Short answers and next steps below.

Lead time & infra touchpoints:
- Hardware/network lead time (customer side): minimal — since Cedarline owns rack/power, our onboarding requires two network endpoints (management + data) and a brief maintenance window for the on‑prem agent install (~2 hours per site). We’ll provide a checklist for the datacenter ops team.
- Blackout windows: Redwood can accept a 48‑hour maintenance blackout per calendar month for each enclave; longer blackout requirements will require a small SLA uplift. Please flag any strict blackout dates.

Pricing / term options:
- We will prepare two priced options: (A) 24‑month reserved with standby amortized across term + 20% seasonal burst pool; (B) 24‑month hybrid reserved + metered burst where standby is billed as reserved baseline + metered overage. Kimberly will attach seat/pricing matrix with concrete numbers.

Action plan: 
1) I’ll escalate this to our Private rollout queue once we get procurement confirmation on the 24‑month preference and the PO cutoff (you said 2028‑06‑28).
2) Priyom will draft an implementation SOW with a June 10th target for site readiness checklist delivery to your ops team.
3) We’ll generate a DocuSign draft for the preferred option (links below) and include the SOW as an exhibit.

JIRA tracking: we’ve created SUP-1123 for the two‑site provisioning (internal delivery tracker) — I'll include Gina’s team on the ticket once we have PO confirmation.

Thanks — will follow up with pricing.

Jordan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procure@cedarline.com>
Date: 2028-05-26T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nested enclave provisioning & contract prioritization for renewal — pricing options

Hi Gina / Jordan —

Attached are two concrete pricing tables and the term-options.csv with amortization models. Summary below (high level):
- Option A (Reserved, amortized standby): 24 months, monthly effective cost = $98,400 (includes 60% standby uplift, 20% seasonal pool), one‑time onboarding $42,500.
- Option B (Hybrid): 24 months reserved baseline + metered burst; effective monthly baseline = $81,200 + metered overage TTM.

SLA note: Because Cedarline requires stricter monthly blackout constraints for analytic re‑runs, Option A includes a standard SLA with a capped maintenance uplift. Option B allows more flexibility but has a higher overage risk.

Next steps we recommend:
- If procurement signs Option A by 2028‑06‑14 we can schedule agent installs starting 2028‑06‑21 and target cutover the week of 2028‑07‑18 (before your July 31 renewal).
- If Option B is preferred we’ll need a PO and a small deposit to reserve the capacity (lead times increase ~2 weeks).

I’ve put a proposed DocuSign envelope together and will wire the template to Jordan for final review.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Nested enclave provisioning & contract prioritization for renewal — PO and timeline

Kimberly / Jordan —

Procurement has reviewed Option A and prefers the amortized reserved model. A few procurement constraints to note: 
- We need contract language specifying data segregation controls and audit log retention (minimum 24 months) before legal signs off.
- PO cutoff: we can issue a PO by 2028‑06‑21 if we receive final DocuSign draft and SOW by 2028‑06‑14.
- Billing request: Cedarline requests monthly invoicing with net‑45.

We will accept the onboarding schedule (agent installs starting 2028‑06‑21) provided the SOW lists the hardware checklist and the blackout allowance. Please include a single exhibit that enumerates the required customer‑side tasks.

Procurement will sign the DocuSign envelope once legal confirms the audit/data language.

Procurement Team

- Kimberly + Legal will update the SOW to include an exhibit enumerating the customer hardware checklist and the 24‑month audit log retention.
- We will surface a specific SLA addendum for the monthly blackout allowance (and any uplift if blackout windows must be extended).
- Jordan will share SUP-1123 and add Gina + Cedarline ops group so you can track delivery milestones.
- DocuSign draft (envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/0a1b2c3d4e5f) will be sent to procurement by 2028‑06‑10 to allow internal legal review before your 6/14 deadline.

I’ll loop in Priyom to start SOW drafting; Kimberly will finalize pricing exhibits. If procurement confirms Option A via a short email, we’ll mark the work as prioritized and lock the 6/21 install window.

Appreciate the speedy coordination — we’ll be in touch with the updated SOW and DocuSign link shortly.
